## 開盤固定收益論點

6月29日收盤部分逆轉週五由中段領漲的溫和行情，殖利率曲線轉為小幅熊市趨平，顯示近期政策限制與長期制度風險的影響有所分化。2年期殖利率上升3個基點，30年期則下降1個基點。這並非殖利率曲線全面重現通膨衝擊，而是風險偏好保持韌性、價格訊號仍偏強，提高了提前寬鬆的門檻；另一方面，市場持續配置長天期實質存續期間，加上聯準會治理風險下降，使長端維持穩定。

10年期殖利率的組成清楚呈現這項分化。實質殖利率下降2個基點，損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點，因此名目指標殖利率持平。實質補償下降，使前一週累積的存續期間利多得以延續；但通膨補償回升，打斷週五較為明確的通膨降溫格局。區域製造業調查顯示，產出與訂單放緩，就業與銷售價格壓力卻明顯增強；西班牙通膨也在能源價格下降之際意外維持高檔。這些訊號使全球政策利率底線仍具限制性，但不足以證明需求正全面加速。

風險資產是第2條傳導管道。美股大幅反彈，半導體重新領漲，波動率下降，市場因而減少前端避險部位。同時，美國最高法院保障現任聯準會理事續任，降低一項原本可能推升美元資產期限溢價的低機率制度性尾端風險。最終，政策時點影響最大的曲線區段走弱；央行獨立性、實質殖利率需求與長期不確定性影響較大的長端則維持穩健。

融資與信用市場運作正常，但實際情況不如平靜的美債收盤所呈現的那麼寬鬆。大規模國庫券標售在7月集中交割前順利完成，投資級私募信貸業者重返債券市場，上市公司債基金也溫和上漲。然而，偏高的股票融資成本可能在季底前占用交易商資產負債表；銀行次順位資本的定價又異常集中，顯示投資人對信用品質差異要求的補償極少。因此，相較週五，核心判斷略有調整：能源價格回落仍有利存續期間，但風險偏好、廣泛且黏著的價格壓力，以及資產負債表競爭，已使眼前壓力重新轉向前端與中段。

## 美債利率、聯準會定價、實質殖利率與殖利率曲線結構

美債表現隨天期拉長而逐步改善。2年期殖利率收於4.10%，上升3個基點；5年期上升2個基點至4.14%。10年期持平於4.38%，30年期則下降1個基點至4.86%。2s10s利差收窄3個基點至28個基點，2s30s收窄4個基點至76個基點。週五5年期債券的相對強勢，因而轉為前端領跌；長端則收復前一交易日的小幅跌幅。

相較前一週的漲勢，單日反轉仍屬溫和。過去1週，2年、5年、10年及30年期殖利率仍分別下降14、15、13及9個基點。單月走勢則更為分化：2年期上升12個基點，5年期僅上升1個基點，10年及30年期分別下降7及13個基點。近端政策預期整月仍偏限制性，中長天期則反映更多經濟放緩、通膨降溫與期限風險緩解。

殖利率曲線曲度也顯示領漲區段已經轉換。2s5s10s蝶式利差上升1個基點至-20個基點，反映5年期相對兩翼回吐週五的部分偏貴程度。2s10s30s蝶式利差下降2個基點至-20個基點，反映10年期相對前端與長債平均水準走強。變動幅度雖小，但足以顯示當日調整集中在政策敏感天期，而非市場全面減碼存續期間。

抗通膨債券定價進一步拆解了10年期名目殖利率持平的原因。10年期實質殖利率收於2.16%，下降2個基點；10年期損益兩平通膨率則升至2.22%。5年及7年期實質殖利率各下降1個基點，分別至1.90%及2.02%；20年及30年期也各下降1個基點，至2.49%及2.68%。各天期實質殖利率普遍下降，顯示短天期名目債券遭到拋售，並非實質期限溢價全面上升。10年期的抵銷力量來自通膨補償回升。

達拉斯聯準銀行調查足以解釋前端為何轉趨審慎，卻未釐清成長前景。6月生產指數下降5點至4.1，新訂單指數由6.4降至2.3，整體企業活動指數持平於零。勞動與價格細項較強：就業指數由0.2躍升至13.9，工時指數升至5.9，製成品價格指數上升10點至28.6；原物料價格指數仍處42.4的高檔。產出放緩削弱需求全面加速的論點，但聘僱與銷售價格偏強，使聯準會仍無法確定限制性政策已經充分發揮作用。

制度風險對較長天期的影響則朝相反方向發展。美國最高法院裁定，聯準會理事Lisa Cook在抗辯總統試圖將其免職期間可以留任，並強調貨幣政策應與政治干預隔離。裁決範圍有限，後續仍可能進入訴訟，但已阻斷透過免職立即改組聯準會理事會的途徑。即使市場原先只反映少量央行自主性風險，威脅下降仍有利於降低長端的治理不確定性補償，尤其當天2年期殖利率仍在反映偏鷹派的總體風險。

國庫券殖利率曲線顯示季底附近出現局部壓力。4週及6週期票息等值殖利率各上升1個基點，分別至3.69%及3.68%；8週期維持3.73%。13週期殖利率上升8個基點至3.83%；17週期上升3個基點至3.88%，26週期上升4個基點至3.97%，52週期上升3個基點至3.96%。壓力集中在3個月以上天期，符合標售供給、交割時點與政策路徑仍具限制性的影響；最短天期則未出現全面性的融資利率跳升。

美國財政部標售$920億91天期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.740%，投標倍數2.32倍，最高利率得標比例85.81%。間接投標人承接$362.93億，直接投標人承接$62.85億，交易商承接$459.97億。另標售$790億182天期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.840%，投標倍數2.58倍，最高利率得標比例96.12%；間接投標人、直接投標人及交易商分別獲配$431.80億、$54.99億及$278.63億。2期國庫券均於7月2日交割。結果顯示市場足以吸收已公布的供給，其中6個月期投標倍數較高，交易商獲配也較少；但真正考驗季底流動性的，仍是其後的現金交割。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

各信用品質層級的上市債券基金均錄得正報酬。LQD上漲0.1826%，HYG上漲0.2255%，JNK上漲0.1871%。投資級與投機級資產同步走高，配合股市反彈及美債長端穩定，顯示企業信用風險未遭全面減碼。不過，發行條件與融資市場狀況仍有明顯差異，未完全反映在基金總報酬中。

Morgan Stanley Direct Lending Fund重返投資級市場，擬發行$3.5億5年期票據，這是該公司1年多來首次發債。初步價格指引約為美債殖利率加245個基點，所得款項將用於再融資，其中可能包括Truist Financial及BNP Paribas提供的循環信用額度。市場近期更加關注私募信貸的放款品質及軟體業曝險，這筆交易因而可檢驗一家企業發展公司能否以債券取代銀行融資。前一週，T. Rowe Price旗下私募信貸基金首次發行$4億債券，最高認購需求超過發行額3倍。這顯示Morgan Stanley交易完成最終定價前，投資人基礎仍然存在。

銀行次順位資本顯示整體需求增強，信用區辨卻轉弱。歐洲大型額外第一類資本債券發行的重設利差標準差，已由1年前超過110個基點，降至2026年略高於52個基點。最寬的新券重設利差由2025年接近1,000個基點壓縮至520個基點；兩年的最窄交易均接近250個基點。美國特別股的利差離散程度也縮減一半以上，降至約46個基點。這些數據顯示，即使銀行的獲利能力與曝險結構不同，投資人接受的補償水準仍日益接近。

利差壓縮並未消除次順位債權的結構性風險。歐元額外第一類資本債券的重設利差集中在300個基點出頭，包括Erste Group一筆交易的307.5個基點；整體平均贖回殖利率為5.85%。經美元避險後，這類債券年初以來的報酬超過3%，逾可比全球投資級指數漲幅的2倍。強勁績效與替代標的稀少可以支撐偏緊定價，但利差離散程度下降，也意味贖回風險、能源密集產業放款及個別銀行獲利能力獲得的明確補償變少。

交易商資產負債表是融資面的主要反向力量。7月S&P 500總報酬期貨合約的融資利差在6月26日一度觸及200個基點，遠高於5月平均的62個基點。大型股票發行、股價上漲及槓桿基金規模擴大，共同增加融資需求。若交易商把更多資產負債表空間配置給股票曝險，美債與附買回市場的中介成本可能上升；此時季底報表要求與附息債交割本已限制交易商容量。

近幾週流入貨幣市場基金的現金有助抑制擔保融資壓力，部分股票融資需求也可能在大型發行結束後消退。不過，到期日較晚的季月期貨，隱含資產負債表成本仍高於5月。這解釋了國庫券標售為何能在未擾動當日附買回市場的情況下完成，也說明7月2日交割為何仍值得關注。信用管道保持暢通，但邊際融資成本日益取決於借款人需要的是銀行額度、公開發債、次順位資本，還是稀缺的交易商中介服務。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

即使能源價格回落，西班牙通膨仍凸顯歐元區面臨的限制。6月整體通膨率維持3.6%，高於3.4%的市場預期中位數，主因電力與天然氣成本抵銷汽油價格下降的效果。全國基礎通膨指標則降至2.9%。整體通膨黏著、核心壓力略為緩和，使歐洲央行仍有空間審慎調整政策，但幾乎沒有理由宣告通膨問題已經結束。西班牙央行預估2026年經濟成長2.3%、2027年成長1.7%，需求韌性也強化了價格訊號。

歐洲其他調查則呈現分歧。歐盟執委會的歐元區經濟信心指標上升1.3點至95.0，就業預期指標則下降2.2點至92.2；兩者均低於100的長期平均。當前信心改善、聘僱計畫轉弱，並未形成單一方向的存續期間訊號。歐洲央行管理委員會成員Martins Kazaks表示，沒有必要在短期內連續多次升息，顯示緊縮步調可以放緩，但政策限制尚未解除。因此，西班牙通膨黏著與就業預期轉弱所指向的，是政策利率底線審慎上移，而非快速緊縮。

英國則出現與通膨無關的買方結構警訊。政治不穩定的影響蓋過高殖利率的吸引力，海外投資人5月淨賣出£55億英國公債，終結自8月以來的連續買超；國內投資人則淨買入£191億，降低整體融資衝擊。約1/3英國公債由海外投資人持有，因此買方替換會影響期限溢價。國內需求可以吸收供給，但財政或政治可信度轉弱時，海外持有人更容易轉向其他主權債市場。

日本的跨境存續期間門檻仍高。日圓在紐約一度貶至每美元161.96日圓，創1986年以來最弱水準，儘管日本央行已在6月稍早把政策利率調升至1%。日圓貶值會提高進口成本與政府干預風險；4月28日至5月27日間，日本政府已投入創紀錄的¥11.73兆支撐日圓。若干預資金來自外國證券部位，可能影響美債需求。與此同時，利差擴大後，日本投資人是否繼續持有海外資產，將取決於避險成本與相對殖利率是否仍具吸引力。

日本消費數據則帶來較強的內需訊號。5月零售銷售月增1.9%，前月數據獲得上修；年增率達5.3%，高於3%的市場共識。藥妝店銷售年增逾7%，便利商店增幅較慢。薪資成長超過通膨，加上政府補貼支撐消費，強化日本央行持續推動政策正常化的理由。不過，補貼也使公布的通膨率低於基礎趨勢，因此民間需求能否持續，比單一整體數字更值得關注。

一名前日本央行高階主管週一受訪時表示，由於金融情勢仍過度寬鬆，日本央行可能在12月前再次升息。他指出，一項基礎通膨指標過去4年平均約為3%，而受補貼壓抑的5月核心消費者物價指數僅為1.4%；他也批評自2027財政年度起仍把每月購債規模維持在約¥2兆的決定。這並非日本央行當前指引，但點出了政策矛盾：日圓疲弱、公布的通膨率受到補貼壓低，而且即使持債規模逐步縮減，央行資產負債表仍會相當龐大。

另有2項日本數據在紐約收盤後公布，因此不能用來解釋當日美債走勢。5月失業率維持2.5%，就業人數較1年前增加52萬人。工業生產月增0.5%，年減1.7%；製造商預估6月產量成長3.7%，7月持平。這些稍晚公布的數據仍呈現分歧的日本公債訊號：勞動市場保持穩定，製造商預期近期生產反彈，但年增率並未顯示產出全面加速。

澳洲則說明，如果未來景氣下行耗盡傳統降息空間，澳洲央行將如何應對。新框架仍以現金利率為主要工具，但保留定期融資、購債、市場操作、前瞻指引、殖利率目標及負利率等額外選項。助理總裁Christopher Kent強調，除了修復嚴重市場失序，這些工具的邊際效果可能有限；資產負債表成本、金融穩定、政策溝通及退場機制也必須從一開始就納入設計。新框架並非當前的寬鬆訊號，而是降低低利率危機下的操作不確定性，同時表明疫情期間採用的固定利率融資、以時間為基準的前瞻指引及殖利率目標，對政策彈性與公共部門資產負債表造成重大風險。

因此，各市場的長天期債券面臨不同限制。西班牙與歐元區同時呈現通膨持續、就業初步降溫；海外投資人轉為賣超後，英國公債更依賴國內承接；日本零售需求轉強，但日圓貶值及政策正常化壓力並存；澳洲則明確區分當前政策與危機工具。這些因素都不要求美國長端殖利率在同日上升，卻說明長天期美債需求仍有條件。海外政策利率、財政可信度與買方組成，隨時可能推高市場出清所需的期限溢價。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

風險偏好升溫、美元走軟，使整體新興市場債券受惠。EMB上漲0.2900%，美元指數下跌0.2466%至101.11。兩者共同改善當日外部融資環境，但並不代表所有主權債同步上漲。油價單月大幅下跌，重新分配進口國與出口國所得；各國政策干預改變本地實質利率路徑，市場融資能力也取決於資本流入結構。

非洲主權債報酬最清楚呈現貿易條件的輪動。Brent原油跌破每桶$73，6月累計跌幅超過1/5，使肯亞及剛果民主共和國債券單月分別上漲2%及1.95%，約為新興市場平均漲幅的2倍。兩國都是石油進口國；對剛果民主共和國而言，燃料成本下降尤其有利於銅、鈷產業及政府補貼負擔。同一波油價走勢則削弱戰時對奈及利亞等出口國的偏好。能源價格下跌雖能改善新興市場整體通膨，卻會擴大國別差異。

印度同時受惠於油價下跌與海外買盤增強。6月期間，外資持有的指數合格政府債券增加3,970億盧比；稅制調整並擴大可納入指數的證券範圍後，當月資金流入可望創下紀錄。一項估計認為，印度最終指數權重將接近0.7%，在分階段納入期間可帶來約$150億被動資金。油價下跌、升息預期消退，已帶動前端債券上漲；下一步則要觀察結構性流入能否把承接力延伸至30年期債券。

巴西則透過財政信貸支持朝相反方向發展。新計畫允許符合資格的非正式工作者以每月1.99%的利率再融資、延長6個月還款期限，適用貸款金額最高為15,000雷亞爾。財政部預估受益人數為20萬至50萬人，信貸由國營Banco do Brasil及Caixa Economica Federal提供。這項計畫可能減輕家庭償債負擔，但也會支撐需求。此時巴西年通膨率仍達4.8%，高於3%的目標，央行又才把Selic利率下調25個基點至14.25%，政策組合使通膨控制更為複雜。

中國則更直接處理半年底融資壓力。中國人民銀行進行人民幣3,000億元隔夜逆回購，另透過7天期操作投放人民幣1,575億元。隔夜利率報1.25%，低於1.35%的市場預測中位數；7天期指標利率維持1.4%。較大規模的隔夜操作旨在平滑季節性流動性，也可能暗示借款成本仍有下調空間。其直接作用是穩定國內貨幣市場，而非改變硬通貨主權債的融資條件。

整體而言，新興市場環境偏多，但各國表現仍具高度選擇性。美元走軟、油價單月下跌，有利廣泛債券報酬與石油進口國；然而，巴西的補貼信貸增加通膨控制難度，印度的存續期間需求部分仰賴政策促成的外資流入，中國則透過央行投放流動性管理融資轉折。主權、銀行體系與企業的傳導管道並不相同，因此個別國家的財政能力及外部現金流創造能力，比廣泛債券基金的單日漲跌更具判斷價值。

## 跨資產

股市對前端賣壓的推升作用，明顯大於對長天期債券需求的衝擊。S&P 500上漲1.1750%，Nasdaq 100上漲2.2546%，費城半導體指數大漲3.8330%，收復前一週部分科技股跌幅。VIX下跌4.1282%至17.65。即時風險趨避明顯下降，與2年及5年期殖利率上升一致，但仍不足以推高10年或30年期殖利率。

能源價格重新帶回少量通膨尾端風險，但沒有扭轉較廣泛的通膨降溫走勢。WTI上漲2.1956%至每桶$70.75，Brent上漲1.6113%至每桶$73.15。美國與伊朗停止相互攻擊、船舶繼續通過荷姆茲海峽後，市場等待雙方重啟談判。過去1個月，WTI及Brent仍分別下跌19.0133%及20.5323%。單日反彈與10年期損益兩平通膨率上升一致；更大幅度的單月跌勢，則仍能解釋前端以外的名目殖利率為何下降。

美元與黃金的走勢不支持系統性避險潮。美元指數滑落至101.11，黃金下跌1.3828%至每盎司$4,022.30。美元走軟與股市上漲並存，緩和即時全球流動性壓力；黃金及波動率同步下降，顯示危機避險需求有限。信用債與新興市場債券基金也溫和上漲，把風險偏好升溫延伸至固定收益資產，但現券利差並未呈現一致變化。

跨資產表現因此解釋了殖利率曲線看似矛盾的走勢。半導體領漲與油價單日反彈，支持政策敏感天期殖利率及通膨補償走高；能源價格單月仍大幅下跌、美元走軟，加上聯準會治理尾端風險下降，使實質殖利率及長債維持穩健。下一步要檢驗的是，風險偏好能否維持強勁，卻不讓銷售價格壓力與交易商資產負債表需求升高到足以中止近期存續期間行情的程度。

## 市場前瞻意義

6月30日至7月2日公布的美國勞動與需求數據，將決定前端領跌是否反映持久的政策壓力。JOLTS職缺與經濟評議會消費者信心指數於週二美東時間上午10:00公布，達拉斯聯準銀行零售業調查於上午10:30接續公布。週三將公布ADP就業、紐約聯準銀行勞動市場緊俏指標、營建支出及ISM製造業指數；週四因假期提前公布的非農就業報告與初領失業救濟金人數，則於上午8:30出爐。若職缺、非農就業與薪資維持強勁，銷售價格或投入價格又再度上升，將驗證熊市趨平，並主要透過2至5年期殖利率、實質利率與預期政策路徑傳導。若聘僱轉弱、訂單下滑且價格受控，則會推翻週一的前端反轉，顯示達拉斯地區就業指數大增只是區域現象，並使前一交易日由中段領漲的存續期間行情重新出現。

歐洲通膨與能源休戰將在7月1日前形成相互連動的全球政策考驗。德國失業數據及消費者物價指數初值於6月30日公布，歐元區調和消費者物價指數初值則在週三出爐。歐洲央行辛特拉論壇連續舉行2天；同一期間，美國與伊朗在杜哈恢復談判，荷姆茲海峽航運狀況也可持續觀察。若各國及歐元區通膨普遍降溫、船舶持續通行，且油價維持單月區間低檔，將證明西班牙整體通膨黏著只是局部現象，降低全球通膨底線，並支撐德國公債、美債損益兩平通膨率下行及石油進口型新興市場主權債。若服務或能源通膨持續、海峽航運再次受阻，或歐洲央行指引強調進一步緊縮，則會推升歐元區前端利率及美國通膨補償。7月1日公布的日本央行短觀調查則增加日本傳導管道：若投資與價格預期強勁，將透過日本公債殖利率及日圓，強化政策正常化壓力。

季底融資將在7月2日交割與美國縮短交易時段迎來關鍵考驗。美國財政部於6月30日標售$800億6週期國庫券，7月1日舉行例行17週期標售；週四美東時間上午11:30再標售4週及8週期國庫券，建議收盤時間為下午2:00。週一標售的91天及182天期國庫券，將在週四上午與非農就業報告同日交割。即使股票融資成本偏高，若現券國庫券殖利率仍然穩定、標售參與廣泛且擔保融資運作有序，就能證明貨幣市場資金流入與交易商容量足以吸收季底轉折。若國庫券殖利率突然大幅上升、交易商承接比例增加，或附買回利率跳升，資產負債表疑慮便會重現，並由前端融資傳導至附息債流動性。若強勁的就業報告在標售前公布，政策重新定價將與本週最大規模的現金及擔保品移轉同時發生，使考驗更加嚴峻。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The June 29 close partially reversed Friday’s controlled belly rally, replacing it with a mild bear flattening that separated near-term policy restraint from long-horizon institutional risk. The 2-year yield rose 3 basis points, whereas the long bond fell 1. That pattern did not signal a renewed inflation shock across the curve. It showed that resilient risk appetite and firm price signals could raise the hurdle for early policy relief even as demand for long real duration and a reduction in Federal Reserve governance risk kept the far end anchored.

The composition of the 10-year yield made the split explicit. Its real yield fell 2 basis points while breakeven inflation rose 2, leaving the nominal benchmark unchanged. Lower real compensation preserved the duration relief established over the previous week, but the rebound in inflation compensation interrupted Friday’s cleaner disinflation mix. A regional manufacturing survey combined slower output and orders with much stronger employment and selling-price pressure, and Spanish inflation stayed unexpectedly elevated despite cheaper energy. Those developments kept the global policy floor restrictive without establishing a uniform acceleration in demand.

Risk assets supplied a 2nd transmission channel. US equities rebounded sharply, semiconductor leadership returned and volatility declined, reducing the need for front-end haven exposure. At the same time, the Supreme Court’s protection of a sitting Fed governor reduced a remote institutional tail risk that could otherwise have raised the term premium on dollar assets. The result was a curve that cheapened where policy timing mattered most and held firm where independence, real-yield demand and longer-run uncertainty carried greater weight.

Funding and credit remained functional, though less complacent than the calm Treasury close implied. Large bill auctions cleared ahead of a concentrated July settlement, investment-grade private-credit financing returned to market, and listed corporate-bond funds advanced modestly. Yet elevated equity-financing costs threatened to consume dealer balance sheet around quarter-end, while unusually compressed junior-bank pricing showed how little compensation investors were demanding for differences in credit quality. The central interpretation therefore changed at the margin from Friday: energy relief still supports duration, but risk appetite, sticky price breadth and balance-sheet competition have shifted the immediate pressure back toward the front and belly.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

Treasury performance improved steadily with maturity. The 2-year yield closed at 4.10%, up 3 basis points, and the 5-year rose 2 to 4.14%. The 10-year was unchanged at 4.38%, while the 30-year declined 1 basis point to 4.86%. The 2s10s curve compressed 3 basis points to 28, and 2s30s narrowed 4 to 76. Friday’s 5-year outperformance therefore gave way to front-led cheapening, while the long end recovered the small loss that had distinguished the previous close.

The daily reversal remained modest against the preceding week’s rally. 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields were still lower over 1 week by 14, 15, 13 and 9 basis points. The monthly pattern was more divided: the 2-year stood 12 basis points higher, the 5-year was only 1 basis point higher, and 10- and 30-year yields were 7 and 13 basis points lower. Near-term policy expectations had retained a restrictive bias over the month even as intermediate and long maturities absorbed more slowdown, disinflation and term-risk relief.

Curve curvature reinforced the shift in leadership. The 2s5s10s butterfly rose 1 basis point to -20 as the 5-year surrendered a little of Friday’s richness against its wings. The 2s10s30s butterfly fell 2 basis points to -20, reflecting the 10-year’s relative strength against the front end and long bond average. These movements were small, yet they place the day’s adjustment in policy-sensitive maturities, not in a broad rejection of duration.

Inflation-linked pricing separated the forces that left the 10-year nominal yield unchanged. The 10-year real yield ended at 2.16%, 2 basis points lower, while the 10-year breakeven rose to 2.22%. 5- and 7-year real yields each fell 1 basis point to 1.90% and 2.02%. Real yields at 20 and 30 years also declined 1 basis point, to 2.49% and 2.68%. The persistence of lower real yields across maturities indicates that the selloff in short nominal notes was not a generalized increase in the real term premium. Inflation compensation absorbed the offset at the benchmark maturity.

The Dallas Fed survey supplied a plausible reason for front-end caution without resolving the growth outlook. Its June production index fell 5 points to 4.1 and new orders eased to 2.3 from 6.4, while the general business activity index was flat at zero. Labor and price details were firmer: employment jumped to 13.9 from 0.2, hours worked rose to 5.9, and the finished-goods price index increased 10 points to 28.6. Raw-material prices remained elevated at 42.4. Slower output reduced the case for a broad demand acceleration, but hiring and selling prices left the Fed with no clean signal that restraint had completed its work.

Institutional risk moved in the opposite direction at longer maturities. The Supreme Court ruled that Fed Governor Lisa Cook could remain in office while contesting the president’s attempted removal, emphasizing the insulation of monetary policy from political interference. The ruling was narrow and left room for further litigation, but it blocked an immediate path to reshaping the Board through dismissal. Removing even a lightly priced threat to central-bank autonomy is compatible with lower compensation for governance uncertainty in the long end, especially on a day when the 2-year still reflected hawkish macro risk.

The bill curve showed localized pressure around the quarter turn. 4- and 6-week coupon-equivalent yields each rose 1 basis point, to 3.69% and 3.68%, while the 8-week yield held at 3.73%. The 13-week yield climbed 8 basis points to 3.83%; 17 weeks rose 3 to 3.88%, 26 weeks added 4 to 3.97%, and 52 weeks increased 3 to 3.96%. The concentration from 3 months onward fit a combination of auction supply, settlement timing and a policy path that remains restrictive, while the shortest maturities avoided a uniform funding jump.

Treasury sold $92 billion of 91-day bills at a 3.740% high rate with 2.32 bid-to-cover and 85.81% allotted at the high. Indirect bidders accepted $36.293 billion, direct bidders $6.285 billion and dealers $45.997 billion. The $79 billion 182-day sale stopped at 3.840% with 2.58 coverage and 96.12% allotted at the high; indirect, direct and dealer awards were $43.180 billion, $5.499 billion and $27.863 billion. Both issues settle July 2. The results established absorption of the announced supply, with stronger coverage and a smaller dealer award in the 6-month sale, but the later cash transfer remains the relevant test of quarter-end liquidity.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Listed credit returns were positive across quality tiers. LQD gained 0.1826%, HYG rose 0.2255% and JNK added 0.1871%. The similar direction across high grade and speculative grade matched the equity rebound and stable Treasury long end, suggesting that the day did not produce a broad withdrawal from corporate risk. Issuer terms and funding-market conditions still showed meaningful differentiation beneath those total returns.

Morgan Stanley Direct Lending Fund returned to the investment-grade market with a proposed $350 million 5-year note, its 1st bond offering in just over a year. Initial price talk was about 245 basis points over Treasuries, and proceeds were intended to refinance borrowings that could include revolving facilities with Truist Financial and BNP Paribas. The transaction tested whether a business development company could replace bank funding after scrutiny of private-credit loan quality and software exposure had increased. A T. Rowe Price private-credit fund’s $400 million debut sale the prior week drew peak demand exceeding 3 times the offering, showing that the investor base remained available before the Morgan Stanley deal reached final pricing.

Junior bank capital revealed stronger aggregate demand and weaker discrimination. The standard deviation of reset spreads on large European AT1 sales had fallen to just over 52 basis points in 2026 from more than 110 a year earlier. The widest new-issue reset spread compressed to 520 basis points from close to 1,000 in 2025, while the tightest deals in both years were near 250. US preferred-share dispersion more than halved to about 46 basis points. These measures describe an investor base accepting increasingly similar compensation from banks with different profitability and exposure profiles.

The compression did not eliminate the structural risk in subordinated claims. Euro AT1 reset spreads were clustering in the low-300s, including an Erste Group deal at 307.5 basis points, and the sector’s average yield to call was 5.85%. Dollar-hedged AT1 returns exceeded 3% for the year, more than twice the gain in a comparable global investment-grade index. Strong performance and scarce alternatives can sustain tight pricing, yet reduced dispersion leaves call risk, energy-intensive lending and bank-specific earnings capacity carrying less visible compensation.

Dealer balance sheet was the principal funding counterforce. The July S&P 500 total-return futures contract touched a 200-basis-point financing level on June 26, compared with a 62-basis-point average in May. Large equity offerings, higher stock valuations and growth in leveraged funds had increased demand for financing. If dealers allocate more capacity to equity exposure, Treasury and repo intermediation can become more expensive precisely when quarter-end reporting and coupon settlements already constrain balance sheets.

Cash moving into money-market funds had helped contain secured-funding pressure in recent weeks, and some equity-financing demand was expected to ease after large offerings concluded. Futures with later quarterly expiries nevertheless embedded a higher cost of balance sheet than in May. The combination explains why bill auctions could clear without a same-day repo disturbance while the July 2 settlement still deserves attention. Credit access remained open, but the marginal cost increasingly depended on whether the borrower needed bank facilities, public bonds, subordinated capital or scarce dealer intermediation.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Spain kept the euro-area inflation constraint visible even after the retreat in energy prices. June headline inflation held at 3.6%, against a median expectation for 3.4%, as electricity and natural-gas costs outweighed restraint from gasoline. A national underlying measure eased to 2.9%. The release combined sticky headline pressure with some core moderation, leaving room for a measured ECB response but little support for declaring the inflation episode finished. Spain’s central bank projected 2.3% growth in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027, adding demand resilience to the price signal.

Broader European surveys were mixed. The European Commission’s Economic Sentiment Indicator rose 1.3 points to 95.0 in the euro area, whereas Employment Expectations fell 2.2 points to 92.2; both remained below their long-run norm of 100. Improving current sentiment and weaker hiring plans do not point to a single duration impulse. ECB Governing Council member Martins Kazaks said there was no need for several increases in quick succession, tempering the pace of restraint without removing it. Sticky Spanish inflation and softer employment expectations therefore favored a higher policy floor reached cautiously.

The UK introduced a buyer-base warning distinct from the inflation debate. Foreign investors sold a net £5.5 billion of gilts in May, ending a buying streak that had run since August, as political instability outweighed the attraction of higher yields. Domestic investors bought a net £19.1 billion, limiting the aggregate funding consequence. With roughly a third of gilts held abroad, the substitution matters for term premium: domestic demand can absorb supply, but foreign holders have more freedom to shift among sovereign markets when fiscal or political credibility weakens.

Japan kept the cross-border duration hurdle high. The yen touched 161.96 per dollar in New York, its weakest level since 1986, even after the BOJ had raised its policy rate to 1% earlier in June. Currency weakness increases import costs and intervention risk, and the government had already spent a record ¥11.73 trillion supporting the yen from April 28 through May 27. Intervention financed through foreign-security holdings can affect demand for Treasuries, while a wider rate differential encourages Japanese investors to retain foreign assets only when hedging and relative yields remain attractive.

Japanese consumption added a firmer domestic-demand signal that became available around the prior publication boundary. May retail sales rose 1.9% from April after an upward revision to the preceding month and increased 5.3% from a year earlier, exceeding the 3% consensus. Drugstore sales gained more than 7% year over year, while convenience-store growth was slower. Wage gains that had outpaced inflation and government subsidies were supporting spending, which strengthened the BOJ’s case for continued normalization; the caveat was that subsidies also held measured inflation below its underlying trend, making the durability of private demand more important than the headline alone.

A former BOJ executive argued in a Monday interview that another rate increase could come before December because financial conditions remained too accommodative. He cited an underlying inflation measure averaging around 3% over 4 years, compared with a 1.4% May core CPI restrained by subsidies, and criticized the decision to keep monthly bond purchases around ¥2 trillion from fiscal 2027. His view was not current BOJ guidance, but it captured the policy tension created by a weak currency, subsidized measured inflation and a balance sheet that will remain large even as holdings shrink.

2 Japanese releases arrived after the New York close and therefore did not explain the Treasury move. May unemployment held at 2.5%, with employment up 520,000 from a year earlier. Industrial production rose 0.5% on the month but fell 1.7% from a year earlier; manufacturers projected a 3.7% June gain and no change in July. The later data preserved a mixed JGB signal: labor conditions remained stable and factories anticipated a near-term rebound, yet the annual production comparison offered no broad acceleration.

Australia clarified how it would respond if a future downturn exhausted conventional rate cuts. The RBA’s new framework kept the cash rate as its primary instrument but retained term funding, bond purchases, market operations, forward guidance, yield targets and negative rates as possible additional tools. Assistant Governor Christopher Kent stressed that their effects beyond repairing severe market dysfunction were likely to be marginal and that balance-sheet cost, financial stability, communication and exit had to be designed from the start. The framework did not signal current easing; it reduced operational uncertainty around a low-rate crisis while making clear that the pandemic’s fixed-rate funding, time-based guidance and yield target created material flexibility and public-balance-sheet risks.

Global duration consequently faced different constraints by market. Spain and the euro area combined persistent inflation with tentative employment cooling; UK gilts depended more heavily on domestic absorption after foreign selling; Japan paired stronger retail demand with currency weakness and normalization pressure; Australia separated current policy from its crisis toolkit. None required a same-day rise in the US long yield. Together they explain why long Treasuries retained demand only conditionally, with foreign policy rates, fiscal credibility and buyer composition still capable of raising the clearing term premium.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Broad emerging-market debt benefited from the risk-on close and a softer dollar. EMB gained 0.2900%, while the Dollar Index fell 0.2466% to 101.11. The combination eased the daily external-financing backdrop, but it did not describe a uniform sovereign rally. Oil’s large monthly decline redistributed income between importers and exporters, domestic policy interventions altered local real-rate paths, and access depended on the structure of capital inflows.

African sovereign returns showed the terms-of-trade rotation most clearly. With Brent below $73 and down more than a fifth during June, Kenyan and Democratic Republic of Congo bonds returned 2% and 1.95% for the month, roughly twice the average emerging-market gain. Both benefited as oil importers, and lower fuel costs were especially relevant to Congo’s copper and cobalt operations and subsidy burden. The same move weakened the wartime preference for exporters including Nigeria, demonstrating that cheaper energy can improve aggregate EM inflation while widening country dispersion.

India paired the oil benefit with a stronger foreign buyer base. Overseas holdings of index-eligible government debt increased by 397 billion rupees during June, putting the month on course for a record inflow after tax changes and an expansion of securities eligible for index inclusion. 1 estimate placed India’s eventual index weight near 0.7% and associated passive inflows around $15 billion over the phase-in. The front end had already rallied as oil fell and rate-increase expectations receded, shifting attention toward whether structural inflows could extend absorption into 30-year bonds.

Brazil moved in the opposite direction through fiscal credit support. A new program allows qualifying informal workers to refinance at 1.99% per month, extend repayment by 6 months and include loans up to 15,000 reais. The finance ministry expected 200,000 to 500,000 beneficiaries, with state-controlled Banco do Brasil and Caixa Economica Federal supplying the credit. The program may ease household debt service, but it adds demand support while annual inflation was 4.8%, above the 3% target, and the central bank had just cut the Selic rate by a quarter point to 14.25%.

China addressed half-year funding pressure more directly. The PBOC conducted 300 billion yuan of overnight reverse repos and supplied another 157.5 billion yuan through its 7-day operation. The overnight rate was reported at 1.25%, below a 1.35% median forecast, while the 7-day benchmark remained 1.4%. The larger overnight operation was timed to smooth seasonal liquidity and may also signal scope for lower borrowing costs. Its immediate channel was domestic money-market stability, not a change in hard-currency sovereign funding.

EM conditions were therefore supportive at the aggregate level and selective underneath. A softer dollar and lower monthly oil prices aided broad returns and importers, but Brazil’s subsidized credit complicated inflation control, India’s duration relied partly on policy-enabled foreign inflows, and China used central-bank liquidity to manage the funding turn. Sovereign, banking-system and corporate channels remained distinct, leaving country-specific fiscal capacity and external cash generation more informative than the daily move in a broad debt fund.

## Cross asset

Equities reinforced the front-end selloff more strongly than they challenged long-duration demand. The S&P 500 gained 1.1750%, the Nasdaq 100 rose 2.2546%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 3.8330%, recovering part of the prior week’s technology decline. The VIX fell 4.1282% to 17.65. This was a clear reduction in immediate risk aversion, compatible with higher 2- and 5-year yields, yet it did not force a rise in the 10- or 30-year yield.

Energy restored a modest inflation tail without reversing the broader disinflation move. WTI rose 2.1956% to $70.75 and Brent added 1.6113% to $73.15, as markets approached renewed US-Iran talks after both sides halted attacks and ships continued through the Strait of Hormuz. Over 1 month, WTI and Brent were still lower by 19.0133% and 20.5323%. The daily bounce fit the rise in 10-year breakevens; the much larger monthly decline remained compatible with lower nominal yields beyond the front end.

The dollar and gold argued against a systemic flight to safety. The Dollar Index slipped to 101.11, and gold fell 1.3828% to $4,022.30. A softer dollar alongside rising equities eased immediate global liquidity pressure, while lower gold and falling volatility showed limited demand for crisis protection. Credit and emerging-market debt funds also advanced modestly, extending the risk-on tone across fixed-income assets without establishing a common cash-spread move.

Cross assets thus reconciled the curve’s apparent tension. Semiconductor-led equity strength and a daily oil rebound supported firmer policy-sensitive yields and higher inflation compensation. The continuing monthly energy decline, softer dollar and reduced Fed-governance tail risk allowed real yields and the long bond to remain firm. The unresolved question is whether risk appetite can stay strong without keeping selling-price pressure and dealer balance-sheet demand high enough to arrest the recent duration rally.

## Forward Market Significance

The US labor and demand sequence from June 30 through July 2 determines whether the front-led cheapening reflects durable policy pressure. JOLTS and Conference Board confidence arrive Tuesday at 10:00 a.m. ET, followed by the Dallas Fed retail survey at 10:30; Wednesday brings ADP employment, the New York Fed labor-tightness measure, construction spending and ISM manufacturing, and Thursday’s holiday-shifted payroll report and claims begin at 8:30. Firm vacancies, payrolls and wages alongside another rise in selling or input prices would validate the bear flattening and transmit most directly through 2- to 5-year yields, real rates and the expected policy path. Softer hiring with weakening orders and contained prices would challenge Monday’s front-end reversal, confirm that the Dallas employment surge was regional rather than broad, and restore the belly-led duration relief seen at the prior close.

European inflation and the energy truce provide a linked global-policy test through July 1. German unemployment and flash CPI arrive June 30, euro-area flash HICP follows Wednesday, and the ECB Forum in Sintra continues across both days as US-Iran talks resume in Doha and shipping conditions through Hormuz remain observable. Broad national and regional disinflation, continued vessel passage and oil holding near its lower monthly range would confirm that Spain’s sticky headline is localized, reduce the global inflation floor and support Bunds, Treasury breakevens and oil-importing EM sovereigns. Persistent services or energy inflation, renewed disruption in the strait or ECB guidance emphasizing further restraint would challenge that interpretation, lifting euro front-end rates and US inflation compensation. The BOJ Tankan on July 1 adds a Japanese channel: strong investment and price expectations would reinforce normalization pressure through JGB yields and the yen.

Quarter-end financing reaches its decisive point at the July 2 settlement and shortened US session. Treasury sells $80 billion of 6-week bills on June 30 and holds the regular 17-week sale July 1, followed by 4- and 8-week auctions at 11:30 a.m. ET Thursday before the recommended 2:00 p.m. close; Monday’s 91- and 182-day bills settle that morning alongside the payroll release. Stable cash-bill yields, broad auction participation and orderly secured funding despite elevated equity-financing costs would confirm that money-market inflows and dealer capacity can absorb the turn. Abrupt bill cheapening, larger dealer retention or a repo-rate jump would reopen the balance-sheet concern and transmit from front-end funding into coupon liquidity. A strong jobs report arriving before the auctions would intensify the test by combining policy repricing with the largest cash and collateral transfer of the week.
